elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Amended Article II grant: "grants to Licensee and, upon written notice to Licensor, its Affiliates and their personnel ... a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology"; AFFILIATE is a defined term (s.1.1).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No reference to contractors or personnel acting on Licensee's behalf; retained restriction (e) still bars use or access "by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee", and the deeming language covers only Affiliate personnel.
The grant remains conditioned on ongoing payment ("provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement") with no perpetual term for paid-up licences.
No irrevocability language was added; the grant remains "subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement" and payment-conditioned.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No edit limits termination grounds to uncured material breach; other termination provisions (Article XX and any other termination events) are untouched apart from the Change of Control sentence.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Article XX(a) as rendered: rights and licences "shall continue in effect and may be transferred to Licensee's successor in a merger or acquisition without Licensor's approval"; the assignment clause expressly defers Change of Control to that section.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Grant now runs "to Licensee and, upon written notice to Licensor, its Affiliates" — coverage is triggered by written notice, exactly as the fallback requires; Licensee is a single named entity so Affiliates were not already included.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Article XX(a) replaced automatic termination with continuation and transfer "to Licensee's successor in a merger or acquisition without Licensor's approval"; p0149 routes any Change of Control to that section, so the general consent bar does not defeat it.

reasons: Fallback is complete: both atomic elements are met in operative language — Affiliates covered on written notice in the Article II grant, and successor transfer on a merger or acquisition without Licensor approval in Article XX(a).

Preferred is not complete: contractors acting on Licensee's behalf are still excluded (and restriction (e) affirmatively bars non-employee access), and no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence or breach-only termination limit was added. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add "and contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant (or conform (e)), state that fully paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, and limit termination of subscription licences to uncured material breach.

The deemed-employee treatment of Affiliate personnel is not gratuitous: retained restriction (e) limits use and access to "employees of the Licensee" and would otherwise expressly contradict the new Affiliate grant, so the conforming words are necessary rather than an extra.

Deletion in Article XX(a) is confined to the automatic-termination and Licensor-consent mechanic that defeated successor transfer; that language was Licensor-favourable, the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition lead-in is preserved, and the p0149 cross-reference to the Change of Control section still resolves, so no dangling term or contradictory retained sentence results.

Original clause correctly classified as a deviation: automatic termination of all licences on any Change of Control (with consent deemed reasonably withheld on broad grounds) plus the employees-only access bar left no path to Affiliates and no successor transfer, failing both fallback elements.
